slides.title: A 75-year-old client arrived at the outpatient clinic for an annual visit. Which
text: Question: A 75-year-old client arrived at the outpatient clinic for an annual visit. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
A. Listen to the client reminisce about the stages of their life and critique accordingly.
B. Discourage the client from repetition while reminiscing about their lifespan.
C. Use open-ended questions to encourage the client to reminisce.
D. Teach the client to reminisce in an orderly fashion.
Correct answer: C. Use open-ended questions to encourage the client to reminisce.
Topic: Health Promotion & Prevention
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Use open-ended questions to encourage the client to reminisce.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Use open-ended questions to encourage the client to reminisce.” – Open-ended prompts encourage recall
Not correct:
• “Listen to the client reminisce about the stages of their life and critique accordingly.” – Criticism inhibits sharing
• “Discourage the client from repetition while reminiscing about their lifespan.” – Repetition can reinforce recall
• “Teach the client to reminisce in an orderly fashion.” – Recall need not follow a strict order
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

text: Question: When a nurse is providing care for a client who has been diagnosed with rubella, the nurse should implement which precaution method?
A. Airborne
B. Contact
C. Droplet
Correct answer: C. Droplet
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Droplet
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Droplet” – Respiratory droplets transmit rubella
Not correct:
• “Airborne” – Used for measles or TB
• “Contact” – Not the main transmission route

slides.title: The nurse is providing care for a client who has scabies. Which of the following
text: Question: The nurse is providing care for a client who has scabies.  Which of the following is appropriate when providing care to this client?
A. Wear gloves when entering the room
B. Wear a mask when within 3 feet of this client
C. Place a mask on the client when taking them to X-Ray
D. Permit no pregnant visitors
Correct answer: A. Wear gloves when entering the room
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Wear gloves when entering the room
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Wear gloves when entering the room” – Contact precautions require gloves
Not correct:
• “Wear a mask when within 3 feet of this client” – Routine mask does not prevent skin transmission
• “Place a mask on the client when taking them to X-Ray” – Transport mask is not needed for scabies
• “Permit no pregnant visitors” – Pregnancy alone is not a reason to exclude visitors
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 1 - Safety & Infection Prevention & Control, slide 10: “Scabies”
• Unit 1 - Safety & Infection Prevention & Control, slide 9: “Gloves”

slides.title: The nursing instructor is teaching a group of nursing students about how to prev
text: Question: The nursing instructor is teaching a group of nursing students about how to prevent the spread of influenza. The nursing instructor identifies further teaching is necessary when a student states,
A. “I will limit the amount of supplies that I bring into the client’s room.”
B. “The client should wear a mask if he/she must leave the room.”
C. “Hand hygiene must consist of soap and water in order to kill the influenza microorganism.”
D. “I will wear gloves, gown, and mask when I enter the room to perform a physical assessment on the client.”
Correct answer: C. “Hand hygiene must consist of soap and water in order to kill the influenza microorganism.”
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• “Hand hygiene must consist of soap and water in order to kill the influenza microorganism.”
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• ““Hand hygiene must consist of soap and water in order to kill the influenza microorgani…” – Alcohol rub is also effective if hands are not visibly dirty
Not correct:
• ““I will limit the amount of supplies that I bring into the client’s room.”” – Limits contaminated supplies
• ““The client should wear a mask if he/she must leave the room.”” – Reduces droplet transmission during transport
• ““I will wear gloves, gown, and mask when I enter the room to perform a physical assessm…” – Appropriate protection for anticipated exposure
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a client diagnosed with Clostridium difficile (C. diff).
text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client diagnosed with Clostridium difficile (C. diff). To prevent the transmission of C. diff, the nurse should:
A. perform hand hygiene with soap and water rather than alcohol based hand sanitizer.
B. assume that only surfaces that the client has touched are actually contaminated.
C. sterilize all of the equipment and supplies that leave the client’s room.
D. wear a mask when in the room and for the client to wear a mask when in public.
Correct answer: A. perform hand hygiene with soap and water rather than alcohol based hand sanitizer.
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• perform hand hygiene with soap and water rather than alcohol based hand sanitizer.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “perform hand hygiene with soap and water rather than alcohol based hand sanitizer.” – Washing physically removes spores
Not correct:
• “assume that only surfaces that the client has touched are actually contaminated.” – Untouched surfaces may also be contaminated
• “sterilize all of the equipment and supplies that leave the client’s room.” – Appropriate sporicidal disinfection is needed, not universal sterilization
• “wear a mask when in the room and for the client to wear a mask when in public.” – Contact rather than droplet precautions
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: The nurse is teaching a new group of unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP) about
text: Question: The nurse is teaching a new group of unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP) about the importance of hand hygiene. Which of the following statements should the nurse include?
A. “If you don’t have an infection, your hands won’t infect others.”
B. “Use an alcohol rub when your hands are visibly soiled.”
C. “Rub all surfaces of your hands with an alcohol rub for 20 to 30 seconds.”
D. “If you wear gloves, you do not have to wash your hands.”
Correct answer: C. “Rub all surfaces of your hands with an alcohol rub for 20 to 30 seconds.”
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• “Rub all surfaces of your hands with an alcohol rub for 20 to 30 seconds.”
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• ““Rub all surfaces of your hands with an alcohol rub for 20 to 30 seconds.”” – Adequate rubbing covers all surfaces
Not correct:
• ““If you don’t have an infection, your hands won’t infect others.”” – Asymptomatic hands can transfer pathogens
• ““Use an alcohol rub when your hands are visibly soiled.”” – Visible soil requires soap and water
• ““If you wear gloves, you do not have to wash your hands.”” – Gloves do not replace hand hygiene
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: A nurse is observing an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP) change the linens o
text: Question: A nurse is observing an unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP) change the linens of a client's bed.  Which of the following observations requires follow-up?
A. The UAP raises the bed to waist level
B. The UAP reaches across the bed to straighten the fitted sheet.
C. The UAP lowers the side rail on the side closest to them.
D. The UAP rolls the client back and forth from one side of the bed to the other to make access easier
Correct answer: B. The UAP reaches across the bed to straighten the fitted sheet.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• The UAP reaches across the bed to straighten the fitted sheet.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The UAP reaches across the bed to straighten the fitted sheet.” – Overreaching strains the back
Not correct:
• “The UAP raises the bed to waist level” – Promotes safe body mechanics
• “The UAP lowers the side rail on the side closest to them.” – Allows access while working at bedside
• “The UAP rolls the client back and forth from one side of the bed to the other to make a…” – Turning the client allows linen placement if done safely
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: The nurse preceptor is observing a new nurse wash their hands. Which of the foll
text: Question: The nurse preceptor is observing a new nurse wash their hands.  Which of the following, if observed, would require the preceptor to intervene?
A. The nurse scrubs in circular motions using lots of friction
B. The nurse washes their hands for 15-20 seconds and sings Happy Birthday to themselves twice to ensure adequate time.
C. The nurse washes their hands as opposed to using hand gel when they notice blood on their palms
D. The nurse allows the water to run off their elbows when washing
Correct answer: D. The nurse allows the water to run off their elbows when washing
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• The nurse allows the water to run off their elbows when washing
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The nurse allows the water to run off their elbows when washing” – Routine washing should drain toward fingertips, not elbows
Not correct:
• “The nurse scrubs in circular motions using lots of friction” – Friction helps remove organisms
• “The nurse washes their hands for 15-20 seconds and sings Happy Birthday to themselves t…” – Adequate washing time is intended
• “The nurse washes their hands as opposed to using hand gel when they notice blood on the…” – Visible blood requires soap and water
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: The nurse is caring for a client who has a Clostridium difficile infection. Whic
text: Question: The nurse is caring for a client who has a Clostridium difficile infection. Which of the following cleansing agents should the nurse use for hand hygiene?
A. Nonantimicrobial soap
B. Alcohol-based hand rub
C. Povidone-iodine
D. Chlorhexidine
Correct answer: A. Nonantimicrobial soap
Topic: Infection Control & Safety
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Nonantimicrobial soap
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)

• “Nonantimicrobial soap” – Soap and water physically remove spores
Not correct:
• “Alcohol-based hand rub” – Alcohol does not reliably kill spores
• “Povidone-iodine” – Not required for routine spore removal
• “Chlorhexidine” – Not reliably sporicidal

slides.title: A client who needs maximum support is ambulating with a cane for the first time.
text: Question: A client who needs maximum support is ambulating with a cane for the first time. After educating the client on proper ambulation with a cane, you assess how well the client understood the instructions. Which findings below demonstrate the proper technique? (Select all that apply.)
A. The top of the cane should be level with the hip joint.
B. The client moves the weak leg past the cane while walking.
C. The arm that is holding the cane is flexed at 40-degrees.
D. The cane should hold the cane 6 inches in front and 6 inches to the side of the stronger leg.
Correct answers: A. The top of the cane should be level with the hip joint.; D. The cane should hold the cane 6 inches in front and 6 inches to the side of the stronger leg.
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• The top of the cane should be level with the hip joint.
• The cane should hold the cane 6 inches in front and 6 inches to the side of the stronger leg.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The top of the cane should be level with the hip joint.” – Proper cane height supports posture
• “The cane should hold the cane 6 inches in front and 6 inches to the side of the stronge…” – Forward and lateral placement provides support
Not correct:
• “The client moves the weak leg past the cane while walking.” – Weak leg advances with cane, not beyond it
• “The arm that is holding the cane is flexed at 40-degrees.” – Elbow should usually flex 15–30 degrees
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: A client who is ambulating with crutches moves both crutches forward along with
text: Question: A client who is ambulating with crutches moves both crutches forward along with the injured leg and then moves the non-injured forward. What type of gait did the client use while ambulating with crutches?
A. Three-point gait
B. Swing-to-gait
C. Four-point gait
D. Two-point gait
Correct answer: A. Three-point gait
Topic: Skills & Procedures
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Three-point gait
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Three-point gait” – Both crutches and affected leg move together
Not correct:
• “Swing-to-gait” – Both legs swing to crutches
• “Four-point gait” – Four separate points advance in sequence
• “Two-point gait” – Opposite crutch and foot advance together

slides.title: Which of the following qualities does the nurse need to provide caring?
text: Question: Which of the following qualities does the nurse need to provide caring?
A. Ability to create a trusting environment
B. Desire to have a stable career and income
C. Sensitivity to the needs of other nurses
D. Longing to help others live a healthy life
Correct answer: A. Ability to create a trusting environment

notes: Rationale:

• Ability to create a trusting environment

Not correct:

• “Sensitivity to the needs of other nurses” – Collegial sensitivity alone does not establish patient trust

slides.title: Which of the following describes the nurse’s role for an older adult client with
text: Question: Which of the following describes the nurse’s role for an older adult client with a chronic illness?
A. Provide caring to help the client live at the optimal level of health and wellness.
B. Suggest that the client accept eventual death to reduce the burdens on the client’s family.
C. Implement an individualized therapeutic regimen that brings about a cure.
D. Encourage the client to minimize the use of services to control costs.
Correct answer: A. Provide caring to help the client live at the optimal level of health and wellness.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Provide caring to help the client live at the optimal level of health and wellness.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Provide caring to help the client live at the optimal level of health and wellness.” – Supports optimal function and wellness
Not correct:
• “Suggest that the client accept eventual death to reduce the burdens on the client’s fam…” – Undermines dignity and autonomy
• “Implement an individualized therapeutic regimen that brings about a cure.” – Chronic illness may not be curable
• “Encourage the client to minimize the use of services to control costs.” – Cost reduction is not the primary goal
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: A 76-year-old is indifferent and responds to others only when they initiate an i
text: Question: A 76-year-old is indifferent and responds to others only when they initiate an interaction. What form of group therapy would be most useful to promote resocialization?
A. Psychotherapy
B. Orientation
C. Reminiscence
D. Activity group
Correct answer: C. Reminiscence
Topic: Mental Health
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Reminiscence
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Reminiscence” – Shared past experiences encourage interaction
Not correct:
• “Psychotherapy” – Focuses on psychological treatment rather than shared recall
• “Orientation” – Targets orientation to person, time and place
• “Activity group” – May engage clients but is less targeted to life review

slides.title: An advance directive gives legally binding direction for health care interventio
text: Question: An advance directive gives legally binding direction for health care interventions when a patient
A. has a new diagnosis of cancer.
B. is diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease.
C. is unable to make decisions for self because of illness.
D. diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is unable to speak.
Correct answer: C. is unable to make decisions for self because of illness.
Topic: Legal, Ethics & Management
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• is unable to make decisions for self because of illness.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “is unable to make decisions for self because of illness.” – Directives guide decisions when capacity is lost
Not correct:
• “has a new diagnosis of cancer.” – Diagnosis alone does not establish incapacity
• “is diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease.” – Diagnosis alone does not establish incapacity
• “diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is unable to speak.” – Inability to speak does not imply incapacity
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 2 - Management of Care, slide 5: “Legal document  that expresses the client's medical decisions should they become unable to do so.”

slides.title: A nurse is caring for a client who has Parkinson's disease and is taking diphenh
text: Question: A nurse is caring for a client who has Parkinson's disease and is taking diphenhydramine 25 mg PO TID. Which of the following therapeutic outcomes should the nurse expect to see?
A. Improved bladder function
B. Delay in disease progression
C. Decreased tremors
D. Relief of depression
Correct answer: C. Decreased tremors
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Decreased tremors
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Decreased tremors” – Anticholinergic action may reduce tremor
Not correct:
• “Improved bladder function” – Anticholinergic effects can cause retention
• “Delay in disease progression” – Does not slow progression
• “Relief of depression” – Not an antidepressant

slides.title: A nurse is providing teaching to the family of a client who has Parkinson's dise
text: Question: A nurse is providing teaching to the family of a client who has Parkinson's disease. Which of the following information should the nurse include in the teaching?
A. Provide client supervision.
B. Speak loudly to the client.
C. Limit client physical activity.
D. Leave the television on continuously.
Correct answer: A. Provide client supervision.
Topic: Neuro, Eyes & Ortho
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Provide client supervision.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Provide client supervision.” – Reduces falls while allowing activity
Not correct:
• “Speak loudly to the client.” – Parkinson disease does not imply hearing loss
• “Limit client physical activity.” – Activity helps preserve mobility
• “Leave the television on continuously.” – Continuous noise may be distracting

The slide's daily exercise program rules out “Limit client physical activity”; supervision is not stated directly.

slides.title: A patient has been admitted after overdosing on acetaminophen. The nurse plans t
text: Question: A patient has been admitted after overdosing on acetaminophen. The nurse plans to monitor this patient for development of which complication related to the overdose?
A. Decreased urinary output
B. Kidney stones
C. Acute hepatic necrosis
D. Metabolic alkalosis
Correct answer: C. Acute hepatic necrosis
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Acute hepatic necrosis
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Acute hepatic necrosis” – Toxic metabolites cause liver injury
Not correct:
• “Decreased urinary output” – Renal injury may occur but is not the hallmark
• “Kidney stones” – Stones are not typical
• “Metabolic alkalosis” – Acidosis may occur, not typical alkalosis

slides.title: The nurse is preparing to administer an injection of morphine to a patient and n
text: Question: The nurse is preparing to administer an injection of morphine to a patient and notes a respiratory rate of 10 breaths/min. What is the nurse’s best action?
A. Hold the drug, record the assessment, and recheck in 1 hour.
B. Administer a smaller dose and record the findings.
C. Notify the health care provider and delay drug administration.
D. Administer the prescribed dose and notify the health care provider.
Correct answer: C. Notify the health care provider and delay drug administration.
Topic: Pharmacology & Labs
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Notify the health care provider and delay drug administration.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Notify the health care provider and delay drug administration.” – Hold opioid and report respiratory depression
Not correct:
• “Hold the drug, record the assessment, and recheck in 1 hour.” – Delays necessary provider notification
• “Administer a smaller dose and record the findings.” – Dose adjustment needs authorization
• “Administer the prescribed dose and notify the health care provider.” – Further opioid can worsen breathing

slides.title: A nurse is making a home visit on a new mother with an infant. What action by th
text: Question: A nurse is making a home visit on a new mother with an infant. What action by the mother requires the nurse to intervene?
A. Shows the nurse the water heater setting that is on 110° F (43.3° C)
B. Keeps hand on infant while reaching for supplies on changing table
C. Places baby to sleep in crib with no blankets, toys, or other objects
D. Cooks while holding and cuddling infant to provide comfort
Correct answer: D. Cooks while holding and cuddling infant to provide comfort
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Cooks while holding and cuddling infant to provide comfort
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Cooks while holding and cuddling infant to provide comfort” – Hot food and surfaces threaten burns
Not correct:
• “Shows the nurse the water heater setting that is on 110° F (43.3° C)” – Low setting reduces scald risk
• “Keeps hand on infant while reaching for supplies on changing table” – Hand contact prevents falls
• “Places baby to sleep in crib with no blankets, toys, or other objects” – Empty crib supports safe sleep

slides.title: The nurse plans a teaching session with a toddler’s parents on car safety. Which
text: Question: The nurse plans a teaching session with a toddler’s parents on car safety. Which will the nurse teach? (Select all that apply.)
A. Place the car safety seat in the front passenger seat equipped with an airbag.
B. Place the car safety seat in the rear seat, behind the driver’s seat.
C. Secure in a rear-facing, upright car safety seat.
D. After the age of 2 years, toddlers can be placed in a forward-facing car seat.
E. Harness safety straps should fit snugly.

Correct answers: B. Place the car safety seat in the rear seat, behind the driver’s seat.; C. Secure in a rear-facing, upright car safety seat.; D. After the age of 2 years, toddlers can be placed in a forward-facing car seat.; E. Harness safety straps should fit snugly.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (select all):
• Place the car safety seat in the rear seat, behind the driver’s seat.
• Secure in a rear-facing, upright car safety seat.
• After the age of 2 years, toddlers can be placed in a forward-facing car seat.
• Harness safety straps should fit snugly.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Place the car safety seat in the rear seat, behind the driver’s seat.” – Rear seat is safer
• “Secure in a rear-facing, upright car safety seat.” – Rear-face until seat height or weight limit
• “After the age of 2 years, toddlers can be placed in a forward-facing car seat.” – Source expects this; only transition after rear-facing limits
• “Harness safety straps should fit snugly.” – Snug harness reduces movement in collision
Not correct:
• “Place the car safety seat in the front passenger seat equipped with an airbag.” – Airbags can seriously injure children
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.
